text:
incident-bot: ALERT: us-west1-primary-gpu queue length > 950 (threshold 300) and 5xx rate rising. Autoscaler attempted 3 scale ops; last error: "scale request rejected: quota_exceeded". Paging oncall-sre. :rotating_light:

oncall-sre: acked. reading metrics now. which customer orgs impacted?

alice: seeing spike in front-door traces -> requests piling in region. many small requests (short seq) but continuous. latency up ~2.1s p95, 429 rate 0.8% overall.

carol: checking autoscaler logs — getting repeated 403 from provider quota API and internal error: "provision_timeout after 6m". autoscaler did not create new instances.

ben (eng-runtime): can we short-circuit routing to us-central1 to relieve the queue? there's a soft-redirect policy but it only triggers after 10m by default. we should force it.

alice: @eng-runtime please execute manual redirect. customers seeing errors now.

eng-runtime: executing manual route update. running command:```
# quick redirect to secondary region
redwoodctl routes set-priority --from us-west1-primary --to us-central1-secondary --weight 0.6 --reason "emergency overflow"
redwoodctl pool adjust --pool us-central1-secondary --tmp-reserve 8gpus --duration 30m
```

incident-bot: ACTION LOGGED: route change initiated by eng-runtime. Config diff link: https://internal.redwood/configs/route-diff/2512345678

dave: I see the route change taking effect in the control plane, but some requests still hit the original pool due to cached affinity keys. we should evict sticky sessions.

eng-runtime: evicting affinity cache:```
POST /internal/affinity/evict
{ "prefix": "us-west1-primary" }
```

carol: autoscaler errors still in logs: provider returned "quota_exceeded" and some API timeouts. I've opened a support ticket with the cloud provider (case #CP-87921). meanwhile the manual redirect should drop queue by ~40-60% based on traffic distribution.

alice: updating status in incident channel and pinging CS for customer impact. @cs-lead can you triage customers for escalation?

cs-lead: on it. initial list: org-42, org-77, and small dev orgs using short-turn models. org-42 reported degraded throughput and some timed-out requests. sending template emails and a direct Slack to their TAM.

oncall-sre: monitoring metrics: queue length fell from 980 -> 420 in 6 minutes after redirect. 5xx rate trending down but still above normal.

ben: we also have an option to spin up a smaller model variant pool (quantized) in us-west1 to accept low-latency traffic while provider quota is resolved. should be fast because model is pre-warmed. thoughts?

alice: do it. prefer less cross-region traffic if possible. favor cheaper quantized variants for non-high-accuracy routes.

eng-runtime: kicking off quick-start of q8 pool:```
redwoodctl model create-instance --model rwd/gpt-small-q8 --region us-west1 --count 4 --labels temp-emergency
redwoodctl routing add-rule --source us-west1-primary --model rwd/gpt-small-q8 --weight 0.4
```

incident-bot: NOTE: temporary q8 pool creation started by eng-runtime. Estimated ready in 90s.

carol: q8 pool is live. traffic shifting. observed per-token cost down and latency back to baseline for the portion routed to q8. still monitoring errors for remaining requests that briefly hit main pool.

dave: double-checking logs: a minority of requests still get 429 from upstream load balancer due to in-flight connection limits. increasing load-balancer backend concurrency to 2000 for us-west1 should help. applying change now.

eng-runtime: applied LB concurrency bump. seeing immediate drop in 429s from 0.8% -> 0.12%.

oncall-sre: good metrics: overall p95 latency stabilizing. queue down to 120. no new scale attempts logged for 12m.

alice: next steps: (1) keep manual redirect active for 1h, (2) keep q8 pool for 2h, (3) cloud provider ticket ongoing for quota increase, (4) postmortem assigned. who owns the postmortem?

ben: I'll take postmortem lead. scope: autoscaler robustness to provider quota responses, routing soft-trigger thresholds, affinity eviction automation, and LB concurrency defaults.

cs-lead: I've flagged impacted customers and started comms. SLA hits: potential for a small number of requests with increased latency and transient 429s between T0 and T0+12m.

carol: ops note: we need a runbook change — reduce soft-redirect delay from 10m -> 3m for primary pool saturation when provider error codes are observed. will propose in postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied. Status: "mitigating". Impact: degraded latency/429s for subset of customers during T0..T0+12m. Next: incident review in 24h.

alice: thanks team. handoff in 30m to next oncall. please add any loose ends to the incident board. :white_check_mark: 

ben: leaving notes for postmortem: capture timeline, include redwoodctl commands we used, provider ticket id CP-87921, and customer comms snippets.

oncall-sre: handing off to night-oncall. I will remain available for 1h if anything regresses. good job everyone. :thumbsup: 

eng-runtime: final note — consider adding a throttling policy that prefers spinning quantized instances automatically for short bursts rather than immediate cross-region redirect. filed RFC: https://internal.redwood/rfcs/371

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: mitigation stable, monitoring for 2h. postmortem assigned to ben.
